sentences.text: This dinosaur is known for a nearly complete skull measuring 48 centimeters, and it is believed to have reached a total length of 13 meters.
The skull is the most complete ever excavated from a titanosaurid, though it is very flattened laterally.
Its teeth were thin and cylindrical with low cutting edges.
The holotype specimen — the specific fossil the species is based on — was found on August 14, 2008, near Coração de Jesus in northern Minas Gerais, Brazil.
Fossils were recovered from the Quiricó Formation in the São Francisco Basin of eastern Brazil.
The genus was named by a research team led by Hussam Zaher in a 2011 publication.
The original describers placed Tapuiasaurus within Titanosauria in the clade Lithostrotia as the sister species to Rapetosaurus in Nemegtosauridae.
Later studies suggested Tapuiasaurus has a distant connection to Nemegtosaurus and a close relationship with other Gondwanan lithostrotians.
Tapuiasaurus lived during the Aptian age of the Lower Cretaceous in what is now Minas Gerais, Brazil.
Tapuiasaurus macedoi is the only known species of this extinct genus, which lived approximately 120 million years ago during the Aptian stage of the Middle Cretaceous in South America.
The time range for Tapuiasaurus is estimated to be between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
A 2016 analysis concluded that the previously found close relationship with Rapetosaurus was an artifact caused by the rarity of skulls in Sauropoda.
